# Task P2-04: Media tools — ffprobe probe, measured quality, fpcalc fingerprint

**Phase:** 2 · **Depends on:** P2-02 (`SoulseekQuality.Infer`) · **Suggested tier:** cheap worker · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal
The import pipeline can ask of any downloaded file: does it decode, what is it really (codec, bitrate, sample rate, bit depth, channels, duration → a measured quality id), and what is its Chromaprint fingerprint — including a second fingerprint from the middle of the file when the first window fails verification. Wraps the bundled `ffprobe`, `ffmpeg` and `fpcalc` binaries behind interfaces so everything above them is unit-testable.

## Deliverables
Namespace `Wondarr.Core.Media`.

1. `src/Wondarr.Core/Media/ProcessRunner.cs` — `IProcessRunner` / `ProcessRunner(ILogger<ProcessRunner>)` (singleton): `Task<ProcessResult> RunAsync(string fileName, IReadOnlyList<string> arguments, TimeSpan timeout, CancellationToken)` → `sealed record ProcessResult(int ExitCode, string StandardOutput, string StandardError, bool TimedOut)`. Uses `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` (never a joined argument string: file names contain spaces, quotes and `…`), redirects stdout/stderr and reads both **concurrently** (no deadlock on large output), `UseShellExecute = false`, `CreateNoWindow = true`. On timeout or cancellation kill the process tree (`Kill(entireProcessTree: true)`) and return/throw accordingly (timeout → `TimedOut = true`, exit −1; cancellation → `OperationCanceledException`). A missing executable (`Win32Exception`) → `MediaToolMissingException` (new) naming the tool.
2. `src/Wondarr.Core/Media/MediaToolsOptions.cs` — config section `Media` (`media:` in `config.yml`, `APP__MEDIA__…`): `FfprobePath` "ffprobe", `FfmpegPath` "ffmpeg", `FpcalcPath` "fpcalc", `TimeoutSeconds` 120, `DecodeCheck` true, `FingerprintLengthSeconds` 120. Validator (keys in messages, e.g. `media.timeout_seconds: …`): timeout 10–600, length 30–300. Register in `AddWondarrCore` with `.Bind(configuration.GetSection("Media")).ValidateOnStart()` — follow how an existing options class is registered (e.g. `MetadataOptions` in `AddWondarrMetadata`); if `AddWondarrCore` has no `IConfiguration`, register it next to `MetadataOptions` instead and say so.
3. `src/Wondarr.Core/Media/MediaInfo.cs` — `sealed record MediaInfo(string Codec, string Container, int? BitrateKbps, int? SampleRate, int? BitDepth, int? Channels, int DurationMs, bool IsLossless, long SizeBytes)`; `static class MeasuredQuality { static long FromMediaInfo(MediaInfo info) }` mapping codec → extension for `SoulseekQuality.Infer` (P2-02, `src/Wondarr.Core/Sources/SoulseekQuality.cs`): `mp3`→`mp3`, `flac`→`flac`, `aac`→`m4a`, `alac`→`alac` (with bit depth), `opus`→`opus`, `vorbis`→`ogg`, `pcm_*` → `wav` or `aiff` by container (`aiff` in `format_name`), `ape`→`ape`, `wavpack`→`wv`, `wmav1`/`wmav2`→`wma`; anything else → 1 (Unknown). Pass `isVariableBitRate: null` (ffprobe cannot tell) — the P2-02 rules then treat a non-standard MP3 bitrate as VBR, as intended.
4. `src/Wondarr.Core/Media/MediaProbe.cs` — `IMediaProbe` / `MediaProbe(IProcessRunner, IOptionsMonitor<MediaToolsOptions>, ILogger<MediaProbe>)`: `Task<MediaProbeResult> ProbeAsync(string path, CancellationToken)` → `sealed record MediaProbeResult(bool Decodable, MediaInfo? Info, string? Error)`.
   - Runs `ffprobe -v error -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <path>`; exit ≠ 0 or no audio stream → `Decodable = false` with the first stderr line as `Error` (e.g. `Invalid data found when processing input`).
   - From the **first audio stream**: `codec_name`; `sample_rate` (string → int); `channels`; bit depth = `bits_per_raw_sample` (string) when > 0, else `bits_per_sample` when > 0, else null — **only for lossless codecs** (`flac, alac, ape, wavpack, pcm_*`); bitrate = stream `bit_rate`, else format `bit_rate`, in kbps rounded; for lossless codecs, the format `bit_rate` (the stream has none for FLAC). Duration = stream `duration`, else format `duration` (seconds as string → ms, rounded). Container = format `format_name` (first item before a comma). `SizeBytes` = format `size`.
   - Then, when `DecodeCheck`, runs `ffmpeg -v error -xerror -i <path> -f null -` and treats exit ≠ 0 as not decodable (`Error` = first stderr line). Skip it when the probe already failed.
   - Ignore attached-picture video streams (`disposition.attached_pic` = 1).
5. `src/Wondarr.Core/Media/Fingerprinter.cs` — `IFingerprinter` / `Fingerprinter(IProcessRunner, IOptionsMonitor<MediaToolsOptions>, ILogger<Fingerprinter>)`:
   - `Task<FingerprintResult> FingerprintAsync(string path, FingerprintWindow window, int trackDurationMs, CancellationToken)`; `enum FingerprintWindow { Start, Middle }`; `sealed record FingerprintResult(bool Success, string? Fingerprint, int DurationSeconds, FingerprintWindow Window, string? Error)`.
   - `Start`: `fpcalc -json -length <FingerprintLengthSeconds> <path>`.
   - `Middle`: fpcalc 1.6 has **no offset option** (`docs/research/research_metadata_plex.md` §2.3), so: start = `max(0, trackDuration/2 − length/2)` seconds; `ffmpeg -v error -ss <start> -t <length> -i <path> -ac 2 -ar 44100 -f wav <temp.wav>` into a unique file under `Path.GetTempPath()` (deleted in `finally`), then `fpcalc -json <temp.wav>`.
   - `DurationSeconds` is **always** `trackDurationMs / 1000` truncated (AcoustID wants the whole track's length, an integer), never fpcalc's `duration` (it is the window's, and 0.00 from stdin).
   - fpcalc exit ≠ 0 → `Success = false`, `Error` = first stderr line (`ERROR: Empty fingerprint`, `ERROR: Could not open the input file (…)`). JSON parse with `System.Text.Json`.
6. `src/Wondarr.Core/Media/MediaToolsHealthCheck.cs` — `IHealthCheck` (see `src/Wondarr.Core/HealthCheck/`): runs `ffprobe -version`, `ffmpeg -version`, `fpcalc -version` once per process lifetime (cache the result in the singleton; checks are resolved per run by `HealthCheckService`, so register the **cache** as a singleton and the check however the others are registered). Ok → "ffprobe, ffmpeg and fpcalc available (fpcalc 1.6.1)" (version from the first line of `fpcalc -version`); missing → `Warning` "Media tools missing: fpcalc — downloads cannot be verified". Register in `AddWondarrCore`.
7. Tests in `tests/Wondarr.Core.Tests/Media/`:
   - With a fake `IProcessRunner` that returns the **recorded** outputs in `tests/fixtures/media/*.ffprobe.json` / `*.fpcalc.json` / `*.stderr` (see `tests/fixtures/media/README.md`): probe of each tone file → exact `MediaInfo` (e.g. `tone-320.mp3` → mp3, 320 kbps, 44100, null bit depth, 2 ch, 3000 ms, quality 29; `tone-v0.mp3` → quality 30 or 24 per its measured bitrate — assert the value the rules give and state it; `tone.flac` → flac, 16, quality 36; `tone-24.flac` → 24, quality 40; `tone-256.m4a` → aac, quality 25; `tone-160.opus` → opus, quality 28); `garbage.mp3` → not decodable with the stderr line; argument lists asserted exactly (including `-length 120`, the middle window's `-ss`/`-t` and the temp file being passed to fpcalc and deleted afterwards); decode-check failure path; `DurationSeconds` truncation (`369999 ms → 369`).
   - `ProcessRunnerTests.cs` — real processes: `dotnet --version` succeeds; a timeout kills (`dotnet` running a long `Thread.Sleep` is awkward — use a tiny inline C# script only if trivial; otherwise run `ping -n 30 127.0.0.1` on Windows / `sleep 30` elsewhere, selected by `OperatingSystem.IsWindows()`), a missing executable throws `MediaToolMissingException`.
   - `MediaToolsLiveTests.cs` — skipped unless `ffprobe` and `fpcalc` are on `PATH` (a custom `FactAttribute` that sets `Skip`): real probe + fingerprint of the tone fixtures. (They run inside the image in P2-18; the dev PC has no ffmpeg.)

## Constraints
- .NET 10, no new packages. No `bash -c`/`sh -c`: run the binaries directly (no shell injection through file names). Never log full stdout of ffprobe at Information (Debug is fine).

## Acceptance criteria (each must be demonstrated)
1. `dotnet build -warnaserror` → 0 warnings, 0 errors; `dotnet test` → all pass (paste the summary lines).
2. The recorded-output tests in 7 pass, with the exact `MediaInfo` for every tone file.
3. The middle-window test shows the temp file created, passed to fpcalc and deleted even when fpcalc fails.

## Out of scope
- AcoustID lookups and the verification decision (P2-05); tagging (P2-06).
